title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
abstract: arXiv:2611.31012v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached an AUROC of 0.87. At a 5% error margin, it could decide for or against emergencies for about half of users. Decision models should therefore not replace triage engines but could shorten symptom assess

translated_title: Jev与开放权重System One决策模型的分诊准确性及其在症状评估应用中用于早期急症识别的研究
translated_abstract: 普通民众越来越多地使用大型语言模型来获取分诊建议，但大型语言模型以多变自由文本的形式作答，这使得难以将其评估用于医疗器械。决策模型会为每个预定义的分诊类别分配概率，因此可能更容易评估。为了测试它们的分诊准确性，我们在233个合成病例和10,000个真实病例上评估了16个决策模型（14个开放权重模型、2个专有模型），共产生了163,728次评估。最佳模型对72.1%的合成病例进行了正确分诊，并在56.1%的真实病例中与现有算法一致。它们在早期识别急症方面更有前景：仅凭人口统计学信息、主诉、危险因素和红旗征象回答，最佳模型的AUROC达到0.87。在5%的错误率范围内，它可以为大约一半的用户做出是否为急症的判断。因此，决策模型不应取代分诊引擎，但可以缩短症状评估
tldr: 该研究对16个决策模型的评估表明，决策模型虽不足以取代传统分诊引擎（最佳模型仅正确分诊72.1%的合成病例），但在早期急症识别上潜力可观——仅凭人口学信息、主诉、危险因素和红旗征象回答即可达到0.87的AUROC，在5%错误率下可为约半数用户判断是否为急症。
en_tdlr: This study of 16 decision models shows that while they are not accurate enough to replace triage engines (the best models correctly triaged only 72.1% of synthetic cases), they hold promise for early emergency recognition, with the best model achieving an AUROC of 0.87 using only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, enabling emergency decisions for about half of users at a 5% error margin.
